findings.documented: Append the API key as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=...
findings.actual: The API key must be sent as an X-API-Key request header. Sending it as a query parameter is rejected with an explicit error telling you to use the header instead.
findings.how_found: First login attempt without the header failed with {"detail":"missing X-API-Key header"}; confirmed query-param style is explicitly rejected on /v1/listings too.
findings.impact: Following the documented auth method as written makes every single request fail.

findings.documented: Response contains a `token` field and expires_in: 86400 (24 hours); no refresh flow exists.
findings.actual: Response contains `access_token` (not `token`) with expires_in: 900 (15 minutes), plus a `refresh_token` and `refresh_url` for a working refresh flow.
findings.how_found: Logged in directly and inspected the raw response; confirmed by decoding the JWT's iat/exp (exactly 900s apart) and by successfully calling /auth/refresh.
findings.impact: A frontend built to the docs (single login, no refresh) would stop working after 15 minutes, failing the assignment's own 30-minute persistence requirement.

findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists, accepts a refresh_token, and returns a new access_token plus a rotated (single-use) refresh_token.
findings.how_found: Called it directly with the refresh_token from login; got a valid new token pair. Reusing the old refresh_token afterward is expected to fail (rotation).
findings.impact: This endpoint is required to build a working app, since real tokens expire in 15 minutes.

findings.actual: user object contains {email} only; no name field is returned.
findings.impact: Minor - any UI relying on a returned user name must fetch or omit it instead.

findings.documented: Collection responses are shaped {total, page, page_size, results}.
findings.actual: Collection responses are shaped {limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results} - offset-based, not page-based, with no page/page_size fields at all.
findings.how_found: First authenticated call to /v1/listings?limit=1 returned this shape directly.
findings.impact: A client built around page/page_size pagination as documented cannot page through data at all.

findings.actual: The server silently clamps limit to 50 regardless of what is requested, with no error or warning.
findings.how_found: Requested limit=200 on every page of a full data pull; every response returned exactly count:50.
findings.impact: A client assuming 200-record pages will silently under-fetch and may miscalculate the number of pages needed.

findings.documented: "total is the exact number of records matching your filters."
findings.actual: Walking /v1/listings fully with no filters yields 4400 unique records (verified no duplicate listing_ids), but the server's own total field reports 4009. The same understatement pattern occurs on /v1/rentals (total=1503, actual walk=1650) and /v1/projects (total=428, actual walk=470).
findings.how_found: Paged every endpoint to completion, then deduplicated listing_id/project_id values to rule out pagination drift as the explanation before concluding total was wrong.
findings.impact: Any client trusting total to know when to stop paging, or to display a record count, under-reports the real dataset size.

findings.documented: "Returns active sale listings ... anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user."
findings.actual: 923 of 4400 retrievable listings (21%) have is_live: false, an undocumented field not present in the sample listing object in the reference doc.
findings.how_found: Inspected raw listing objects for a field not in the documented schema, then counted is_live true/false across the full pulled dataset.
findings.impact: A frontend trusting the docs would display inactive/withdrawn listings to end users as if they were live and bookable.

findings.documented: "Timestamps: ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API."
findings.actual: posted_at on listing (and rental) records has no Z suffix and no offset at all (e.g. "2026-08-29T20:53:00"), and appears to represent bare local IST wall-clock time, consistent with the server's own /health endpoint reporting its clock in Asia/Kolkata (+05:30).
findings.how_found: Checked /health first (documented UTC/Z claim also does not hold there - server_time carries an explicit +05:30 offset), then inspected posted_at on real listing records and found no timezone marker of any kind.
findings.impact: Any client computing time windows (e.g. "posted in the last 7 days") using a UTC assumption as documented would compute the wrong window by 5.5 hours.

findings.actual: Returns 404 {"detail":"Not Found"} - the generic framework 404, distinct from the specific custom error bodies returned by real endpoints, confirming the route does not exist.
findings.how_found: Called the documented path directly, then tried plausible neighboring paths (/v1/analytics, with a locality query param) which also 404'd.
findings.impact: The required Insights screen cannot be built by calling this endpoint; aggregates must be computed client-side from pulled data.

findings.actual: price_min and price_max values are bounded in a narrow 1-99.9 range across all 470 projects (nowhere near real rupee prices, which run into the tens of millions), and price_max < price_min for 348 of 470 projects (74%). The documented field also has no correlation with real prices of listings actually linked to that project (checked directly).
findings.how_found: Computed summary statistics for price_min/price_max across the full projects dump, found the majority-inverted min/max relationship, then cross-checked the top projects by documented price_max against the top projects by real linked-listing price and found no overlap at all.
findings.impact: The 'costliest project' cannot be determined by trusting this field; it must be derived from real listing prices linked to each project.

findings.documented: "total_listings ... is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns."
findings.actual: Comparing each project's total_listings field against the actual count of its linked live (is_live: true) listings in the full pulled dataset, 129 of 470 projects (27%) disagree.
findings.how_found: Grouped all pulled listings by project_id, counted live listings per project, and compared against each project's own total_listings field.
findings.impact: A dashboard trusting this field would show an incorrect listing count for over a quarter of all projects.

findings.documented: (implicit - a listing object describes a real, physically possible property)
findings.actual: 40 listing records describe physically impossible properties, in four independent categories of exactly 10 records each: negative price, carpet_area greater than super_built_up_area, floor greater than the record's own total_floors, and non-plot properties (apartment/villa/independent house) with bedroom <= 0.
findings.how_found: Tested several independent impossibility rules against the full listings dump; confirmed the four groups are fully disjoint (union = 40) and manually inspected sample records under each rule.
findings.impact: These records cannot represent real inventory and would need to be excluded from any user-facing display or aggregate calculation.

findings.documented: (implicit - each listing's posted_by_contact identifies its genuine seller/agent)
findings.actual: 261 listings are attached to one of a set of phone numbers that is also attached to multiple different posted_by_name values, all under posted_by: "agent". A single real person or agency does not operate under a rotating set of different names on one number; legitimate owners/builders/agents in the same dataset consistently use one name per number.
findings.how_found: Grouped all listings by posted_by_contact, found the baseline maximum listings-per-number for owner (8) and builder (6) postings under a single consistent name, then found agent-attributed numbers repeating up to 32 times across 3-6 different names each.
findings.impact: These listings likely exist to generate enquiries rather than represent real inventory for sale, and should be flagged or excluded in any user-facing view.

findings.documented: GET/POST /v1/favourites and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} let a logged-in user save, list, and remove favourite listings.
findings.actual: All three operations return the generic framework 404 {"detail":"Not Found"}. Confirmed against every plausible variant: GET and POST on /v1/favourites, the American spelling /v1/favorites, no-prefix /favourites, /v1/me/favourites, and /v1/user/favourites - all 404 identically.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/favourites directly while building the Saved Listings screen; when it 404'd, tested spelling and path variants and POST before concluding the endpoint doesn't exist at all.
findings.impact: The required 'saved listings' feature cannot be built against the real API as documented; had to fall back to per-user local storage.
